Author: Meric
Message:
feat(stellar): deploy the spend vault to Stellar mainnet and publish the proof

AgentSpendPolicy is live on pubnet at CB5LYXFKKTKDDSCM6JO6C4GNRQUFBGSLYDET6Q56JNFJQSMBKH6KWSYP,
holding real Circle USDC. The receipt is soroban/releases/pubnet-v0.1.0.json and
every hash below is on the public ledger.

What the deploy proves, in the contract's own terms:

- An agent spent 0.20 USDC inside a 0.25 per-payment ceiling, then three more at
  exactly the ceiling, taking spent_today to 0.95 of a 1 USDC daily cap.
- The next payment was refused with DailyCapExceeded. That refusal is the one
  worth reading: the vault held only 0.05 USDC at the time, so InsufficientBalance
  was also available, and the contract returned the CAP error because the cap gate
  fires at policy.rs:89 and the balance gate at 121. The order is the product. An
  agent told its budget is spent needs a different human response than one told
  the account is short.
- A 0.50 USDC attempt was refused with AboveAutoApprove, and a payment against a
  frozen vault with Frozen. Neither has a transaction, because Soroban answers
  refusals during simulation and submits nothing. The typed code is the artifact,
  and anyone can reproduce it against the live contract for free.
- The owner then paid straight through the freeze with owner_pay, and it still
  counted against the daily cap: the override bypasses the gates, not the budget.

spent_today came to rest at exactly the daily cap. The vault spent its whole
budget for the day and refused the next unit, which is the sentence this contract
exists to be able to make on mainnet rather than in a test.

The wasm hash is byte for byte the testnet vault's, so mainnet runs the code that
has been under test since 2026-08-15 rather than a rebuild of it.

Provenance and the registry:

- provenance.ts gains a `stellar` entry, and PROOF_RAILS' stellar rail now spans
  both networks, so /proof/stellar shows mainnet and testnet side by side with a
  live contract read against each. Verified: pubnet reads deployed at ledger
  64103672.
- The pubnet descriptor moves planned -> beta, and beta is deliberate. The policy
  is enforced on mainnet and real money moved under it, but no paid call SELLS
  there yet. In this repo live means wired AND carrying traffic.
- The USDC SAC was verified the way the testnet one was, plus one step that only
  matters on mainnet: Horizon lists dozens of assets called USDC because anyone
  may issue one, so the ISSUER was checked first and its home_domain is
  circle.com. The SAC id was then derived from that asset plus the pubnet
  passphrase, and read back live for symbol, decimals and name.

One bug fixed on the way, found by adding the network rather than by review:
chains/proof.ts told readers to check the wasm with `stellar contract fetch
--network testnet`, hardcoded. Against a pubnet contract that returns "not found",
which reads as our evidence being fake rather than as a typo in our docs. The
network is now derived from the networks the page is actually showing.

Six tests moved, and each was written to be moved. "pubnet is the only Stellar
network still planned" said it would stay planned "until a capped vault is
deployed and money that matters has moved through it"; that happened, so it now
asserts no Stellar network is planned and checks the two SAC ids differ, since a
shared id would mean one was pasted. The facilitator test that asserted
unavailable[0] now looks up by network: pubnet declaring a SAC took that slot,
which is the facilitator being more honest, not less.

Cost, since this spent real money: 21 XLM in, 12.3812765 XLM of network fees
(12.23 of it the wasm upload alone, which pays rent for its 11,625 bytes), 5.1
XLM swapped to 1 USDC on Stellar's own order book. The remainder and the USDC are
still held. Burner keys, generated for this deploy, named in the release record.

816/816 backend tests, tsc clean, lint 0 errors, build green.

Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: Meric
Message:
feat(soroban): the SoW evidence pair on testnet, and what the second half actually took

AgentSpendPolicy is deployed on Stellar testnet at CAIL6ECR...B4UI and both halves of the
Instawards success metric are real transactions, verified against Horizon rather than
against the tool that produced them.

  under-limit payment settles   3da74634...  successful, ledger 4147945
  over-limit payment refused    12df418f...  FAILED,     ledger 4147972

The first moved 1 USDC inside a 2 USDC ceiling and a 10 USDC cap; the payee's classic
balance really went to 1.0000000. The second is in the ledger and carries the contract's
own error: invokeHostFunctionTrapped with a diagnostic event of Error(Contract, #5), and 5
is DailyCapExceeded in the frozen table in error.rs.

The second half is the interesting one, and the plan predicted the risk without predicting
its shape. The worry was that a typed error might not render legibly on stellar.expert. It
renders fine. What is actually true is stranger: a refused payment normally produces NO
TRANSACTION AT ALL. Every Soroban client simulates first, so a call the contract refuses
fails in simulation and nothing is submitted. `stellar contract invoke` will not send it
even with --send=yes. --build-only emits a transaction with no Soroban resource footprint
and the network rejects it as TxMalformed. And the hash the CLI prints in that case
resolves to 404 on Horizon: it is a local computation of something that never existed.

On EVM a revert is still a mined transaction with a hash you can open. The metric as
written assumes that shape, and on this platform it does not hold.

The honest way through is to make the payment fail at APPLY time instead of at simulation,
which happens whenever the policy tightens between the moment the agent builds its payment
and the moment the ledger includes it. That is not a contrivance to satisfy a checkbox: it
is exactly the race a real agent hits when a human moves the limit mid-flight, and it
demonstrates the product better than a static refusal would. The transaction is included,
it pays its fee, and it is recorded as failed with the contract's own code.

Also worth recording, because it cost time and would cost more on mainnet: testnet USDC
came from the Stellar DEX rather than a faucet, about 11 XLM for 20 USDC through a path
payment, so no rate limit and no third party. And the first faucet attempt went nowhere
because neither classic account had a USDC trustline. A payment to an account without one
fails outright; nothing is held anywhere. The vault itself needs none, since contract
balances live in contract storage, but every classic payee does.

The SAC was derived with `stellar contract id asset` and matched the constant @x402/stellar
exports, then read live for decimals 7 and symbol USDC. Three independent agreements before
a single unit moved. releases/testnet-v0.1.0.json carries all of it, plus the caveats.

Author: Meric
Message:
fix(chains): a signer key with a stray newline is a key, not a 502

The deployed rail refused every settlement with viem's "invalid private key,
expected hex or 32 bytes, got string". The key was fine; it had whitespace
around it, which is what happens when a key is pasted into a hosting
dashboard's text field. The old code handed the raw string to viem, so the
buyer got a raw library error about a problem they could not see or fix.

Keys are now trimmed and shape-checked before use. Anything still unusable is
treated as no key at all, which is what the honesty rule already requires of a
missing credential: a clean labeled no-op, never a crash. It is also logged
loudly and names the chain, because a signer that is silently absent is a
configuration error nobody would otherwise find.

Author: Meric
Message:
feat(x402): a first-party EIP-3009 facilitator, and Robinhood Chain goes live

Robinhood Chain had no x402 facilitator from anyone, so a seller there could
not accept a gasless payment at all. This adds one, and it is stronger than the
rail it learned from: the buyer signs a transferWithAuthorization and pays no
gas, we broadcast it, and "settled" means a receipt we hold carrying a matching
Transfer log, not a third party's word.

The signing domain is proven rather than pasted. USDG exposes no version() and
no eip712Domain(), so the domain cannot be read; instead each candidate is
rebuilt and only the one reproducing the live DOMAIN_SEPARATOR is accepted, and
an unprovable domain serves no challenge at all. Four real settlements now sit
on chain 4663, one per sellable tool, the first at 0xbb41c7aa in block 35439881,
which is why the descriptor flips from beta to live. Gas measured at 102495 per
settlement, and the settlement fee is disclosed as its own line item rather than
hidden in a marked-up price.

USDG is named in a new settlementTokens field, never in contracts.usdc: that
slot is what payUsdc, the escrow approve and the vault constructor read, and
pointing it at a token they were never tested against is exactly the mistake the
old test was written to prevent. /settle is allowlisted because we pay the gas;
/verify and /supported are open.

Alongside: the chain sweep that stops surfaces lying about the ten chains, from
the resolve_agent enum that rejected six real chains to llms-full.txt still
calling Robinhood undeployed.

Author: Meric
Message:
feat(celo): the trust oracle learns a new chain, and pays its gas in dollars

Celo joins the registry as a live pair: mainnet moves to beta with the
verified ERC-8004 registries (the same CREATE2 addresses the codebase
already trusts on X Layer and Arc), honest notes where Celo differs (no
ValidationRegistry yet, so KYA anchoring is stated as impossible rather
than faked), USDm replacing the retired cUSD name, and a celo-sepolia
descriptor with the current testnet endpoints, Alfajores being deprecated.

A new fail-closed x402 rail sells the four trust tools on Celo through
the first-party facilitator: a v2 exact challenge priced in native USDC,
verify then settle with no resubmission on ambiguity, every settlement
recorded in a durable proof log, and a 501 rather than a free answer
when credentials are missing. reputation_score reads Celo's on-chain
ReputationRegistry live so a paid call returns chain truth, not vibes.
The public /celo-proof page renders the log with internal traffic
labeled, because the judges screen for sybil and our defense is
transparency. Register and buyer scripts ship prepared-or-executed,
with ERC-8021 attribution suffixes and CIP-64 USDC gas.

Suite at 498 across 39 files; e2e, http-smoke, prerender (35 routes),
build gates, and the 21-route browser smoke all green.

Author: Meric
Message:
harden: close authz, x402-binding, DoS, SSRF, and on-chain custody gaps

Security/correctness hardening pass across backend, frontend, and contracts.
Verified: backend 87/87 unit tests, E2E 39/39, frontend typecheck+build,
live SIWE HTTP proof 8/8, browser UI drive (Playwright+Chromium) 12/12.

Backend
- authz: /api/wallets/assign is now owner-gated (ownsAgent); was unauthenticated
- x402: bind redemption to the payer (signed nonce + on-chain `from` match)
- x402: fail-closed spent-set hydration + per-hash in-flight guard (replay/TOCTOU)
- reputation/risk: tenure only from platform createdAt, not the self-hosted tokenURI;
  NaN-date guard; identity.valid no longer read from the agent-controlled tokenURI
- input validation: reject negative/NaN amounts; clamp permissions; 256KB body cap
- rate limiting: derive the client IP from a trusted-proxy X-Forwarded-For hop
- demo/agent-run: cap client-chosen USD amounts (they spend the shared signer)
- autopilot: include the protocol fee in the budget check
- session tokens carry exp (default 7d) and are rejected once expired
- SSRF guard on the tokenURI fetch (block private/metadata IPs, redirect:error)
- vault: require a human/Safe owner distinct from the operator; in-flight guard
- remove server-side wallet key generation over HTTP (no-custody only)
- /stats reads PAY_TO_ADDRESS instead of a hardcoded literal
- CORS: allow the x402 payment headers so cross-origin redemption isn't blocked

Contracts
- MerkleAirdrop: sweep disabled until an immutable claimDeadline (recompiled)

Frontend
- x402: switch the wallet to Arc before sending; sign the payer-binding challenge
- fetch-race cancellation guards on Wallet/Settlements/Permissions loaders
- clamp negative money inputs

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
